subject: Azure private offer renewal — migration credit allocation and SLA exception request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Gina Ramos <procurement@helixtx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private offer renewal — migration credit allocation and SLA exception request

Hi Gina,

Following up on our renewal for Helix’s Azure private offer (deal D-98321-AZ). We’ve put together an updated Private Offer draft that reflects the term extension and the two items you asked us to confirm during last week’s call:

- One-time migration credit of $120,000 to offset the cost of the upcoming data migration (applied as an invoice credit across the first two billing tranches).
- An SLA exception for the scheduled maintenance window tied to the data migration cutover (we propose a 72-hour planned maintenance window where the standard availability SLA will be suspended for rolling cluster updates).

Attached: Helix_PO_Draft_2028-04-02.pdf (redlined) and sla-exception-request.docx.

Proposed timeline:
- 2028-04-08: Finalize PO language and sign-off from Helix procurement.
- 2028-04-15: DocuSign circulation for Redwood signature.
- 2028-05-01: Migration kickoff (migration credit begins to apply to first invoice tranche).

Questions we need answered from your side to lock schedules:
1) Can Helix procurement confirm the billing entity (Helix Therapeutics US Inc. or Helix Therapeutics Global)? That affects the private offer tokenization on Azure.
2) Legal to confirm whether the SLA exception draft is acceptable or if you need additional audit language.
3) Any preference on invoice proration vs. credit line application (we recommend invoice credit to simplify marketplace reconciliation).

Ben (cc’d) will provide the final billing cadence and confirm marketplace mechanics (how credit will appear on Azure invoices). Marissa will loop in Marketplace Ops to pre-authorize the private offer update.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if that helps.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0183

Attachments: Helix_PO_Draft_2028-04-02.pdf (draft PO, redlines), sla-exception-request.docx (SLA language)
From: Gina Ramos <procurement@helixtx.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Therapeutics Legal <legal@helixtx.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer renewal — migration credit allocation and SLA exception request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the draft and the clear timeline. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:

- Billing entity: Helix Therapeutics US Inc. (confirmed).
- Migration credit: Procurement prefers a line-item credit applied to the first two invoices rather than proration, but legal will confirm if that complicates marketplace acceptance.
- SLA exception: Legal flagged one sentence about liability during the maintenance window — they asked us to request a short paragraph that states: Redwood will provide a written maintenance plan 10 days prior and a rollback plan within 24 hours if critical availability impact occurs.

We’ll aim to get legal comments back by EOD Wednesday (2028-04-04). Also copying AWS seller support to confirm whether a two-tranche invoice credit is supported on the Azure private offer flow (we had some confusion with Marketplace mechanics previously).

Quick ask: can Redwood produce an invoice sample showing how the $120k credit will appear across the two tranches? That will speed approvals.

Appreciate it —

Gina Ramos
Head of Procurement, Helix Therapeutics
procurement@helixtx.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Gina Ramos <procurement@helixtx.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer renewal — migration credit allocation and SLA exception request

Hi Gina — quick reply with the marketplace mechanics and an invoice sketch attached.

Summary:
- Billing entity: noted as Helix Therapeutics US Inc. — we’ll ensure the private offer targets that entity id.
- Credit application: Azure private offer supports invoice credits delivered as negative line-items on the seller invoice that flow through the invoice reconciliation process. In practice we apply the credit as two negative line-items: $60,000 on the first invoice and $60,000 on the second. This is the approach that aligns with Helix’s preference.
- SLA exception: Redwood can accept the two-paragraph modification proposed by Helix legal (maintenance plan + rollback within 24 hours). We’ll have Legal review the exact wording; Jordan will own escalation if Legal requests additional indemnity language.

Attached: invoice-sample-Helix-2028-04.xlsx (sketch) and Helix_PO_Draft_2028-04-02.pdf (copy with marketplace targeting flagged).

Next steps / action owners:
- Helix procurement (Gina): confirm acceptance of the two-tranche credit on record.
- Helix legal: provide final SLA exception wording by EOD 2028-04-04.
- Redwood (Marissa): pre-authorize marketplace ops to apply the updated private offer once doc signs.
- Redwood (Jordan): monitor legal and escalate to marketplace support if marketplace validation fails.

I’ve also dropped the HubSpot deal link here for your convenience: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/D-98321-AZ (shows the PO draft and signatures).

Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Azure private offer renewal — migration credit allocation and SLA exception request

Hi Gina — great, thank you for the quick turn.

Confirming next steps per today’s thread:
1) Helix legal to send final SLA exception wording by EOD 2028-04-04. If we don’t receive redlines by then, Redwood will insert the proposed maintenance + rollback paragraph and proceed to DocuSign.
2) Helix procurement confirms the two-tranche invoice credit (we noted US billing entity).
3) Once legal confirms wording, Redwood will update the Private Offer and circulate via DocuSign. Expected DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/placeholder-helix-98321
4) Marketplace ops (Marissa) will pre-authorize the private offer change to avoid acceptance delays on the Azure side.

Gina — if everything above is good, I’ll send the DocuSign packet Friday morning and Ben will confirm the invoice appearance.

Thanks — looking forward to closing D-98321-AZ and coordinating the migration window.

Soojin Lee
